correctness.rationale: Nonnegative copula density and orthonormal mean-zero functions give valid stationary Markov transition. Exact calculation of its powers yields lag products; each lag quadratic form is a signed weighted forest adjacency with sign-symmetric spectrum and attained Rayleigh endpoints. Finite sample covariance counts give \(H_N\) including \(N=1\), the complement carries eigenvalue one and unit diagonal brackets this, and operator-norm convergence gives H. The Fourier example has positive density and exact correlation \(\sqrt2/8\) > \(1/8\); exact eigenvalues \((33\pm\sqrt{129})/32\) and \(15/16\) follow by invariant symmetry sectors. An actual executable standalone checker passed 718 finite assertions incl independent quadrature, corroborating but not replacing the proof.

originality.rationale: Full public source Longla (2026), Theorem 4.4(2) and its proof assert a half-maximum adjacent common-score correlation bound, while equations (11), Theorem 5.1 and the source trigonometric two-dependent example allow adjacent coefficient interference. Exact Rayleigh optimization yields the sharp signed path spectra at every lag and the attained finite-horizon/long-run variance envelopes, which the source neither states nor proves. The explicit admissible witness contradicts the published bound. Longla (2025) is confined to idempotent and one-dependent families. Classical Kac-Murdock-Szego results cover the abstract constant-coefficient Toeplitz matrix, not this statistical identification or the false sharp same-score assertion. Relevant indexed searches did not locate a specialized correction. Residual risk: unindexed equivalent work and general operator-theoretic corollaries.

value.rationale: A currently published universal covariance bound for this natural finite-memory statistical model is false, and the correction is an attained all-lag, all-sample-horizon classification rather than a single cheap falsifying number. For the valid two-dependent example the peak lag correlation \(\sqrt2/8\) exceeds the asserted \(1/8\) by a factor \(\sqrt2\), and across homogeneous longer paths the factor approaches two. Exact eigenvalue intervals identify the score functions of largest and smallest long-run effective variance, directly relevant to sample-mean inference and dependence-robust uncertainty quantification. Both over- and under-dispersion extrema are established for every admissible parameter sequence.
